extracted.intended_audience: members of the public (citizens, advocates, interested individuals) who want to submit comments on proposed federal regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Practical step-by-step guidance for members of the public on finding proposed federal rules (Federal Register/Regulations.gov), preparing comments, and submitting them during the notice-and-comment period. Covers how to identify the rule, locate its docket, required submission fields, acceptable file types, and tracking submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and comment period
rubrics_metrics.description: Public comment is given during the 'proposed rule' stage; the public comment period generally lasts 60-90 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comments within the stated deadline shown under the proposed rule's title in the Federal Register; check the specific last date for submitting comments for each rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know your rule / identify which rule to comment on
rubrics_metrics.description: To comment on a proposed rule, you must first know which rule you would like to comment on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn about proposed rules via newspapers, magazines, media coverage, and public interest organizations; the most complete source is the Federal Register, which lists all proposed rules open for comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Federal Register to find proposed rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Register is published every weekday and includes all proposed rules open for public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the Federal Register entry for a proposed rule to find the comment deadline and other essential details; the site recommends tips for reading the Federal Register and points to gpoaccess.gov for online access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find the rule and related documents on Regulations.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: On Regulations.gov you can search for rules, comments, and documents by entering keywords, browse by topic, and view rules grouped by comment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refine searches using options on the left side (agency, document type, etc.); be aware search returns specific documents (proposed rule, studies, comments) rather than a single 'rule' record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the docket to track a rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: A collection of documents related to one specific rulemaking is called a docket; the docket shows all documents related to a specific rule and provides the link to comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finding the docket link is valuable for tracking a rule or submitting a comment. Note: Regulations.gov does not provide a way to search for dockets directly, but each search result includes a link to the docket that document belongs to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirements and public visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To submit comments you will be required to provide your first and last name, city, state and country; all other fields are optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep in mind that much of the information you provide will be publicly viewable on Regulations.gov; consider privacy when filling optional fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment content: scope, depth, and focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Your comments can be brief or in-depth and well researched; they can address only specific aspects of the proposed rule, fully address all aspects, or address the subject at-large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies often ask the public to comment on specific aspects of a proposed regulation, but you may comment on any part or the whole regulation. Choose scope and depth based on your expertise and the agency's requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachments and accepted file types
rubrics_metrics.description: You may upload your comments by adding an attachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations.gov accepts all common file types including Microsoft Word documents and Adobe PDF files; use attachments when you have longer, formatted, or supporting documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment tracking and review
rubrics_metrics.description: After submitting your comments you will be provided with a comment tracking number so that you can review your comments after the appropriate agency has reviewed and posted them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the tracking number to monitor whether and when your comment appears and to reference your submission in follow-ups.
